trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up-left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down-right.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-left.
The line must go down-left: up-left is number 18, which comes later; left is number 17, which comes later.
Going down-left would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going down-right would turn number 6 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (-3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Number 11 is only reachable this way.
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going up-left would turn number 13 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going up-right would strand number 13: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
I can't rule out down-right or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-right.
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 14; going up-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down-right.
Going up-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
The line must go up-left: up-right is number 17, which comes later.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 17 before its turn. So the line goes up-left.
Going right would force the line onto number 17 before its turn; going up-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 16. So the line goes up-left.
Going up-left would wall in number 19, the last number; going up-right would cut off the top edge (2 cells). So the line goes right.

Going up-right would leave both cell (1,-3) and cell (3,-3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-left would cut off the top edge (2 cells) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-right.
Going up-right would leave both cell (3,-3) and number 18 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Cell (3,-3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 31 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 36/37 cells (97%).
Generation 3: fitness 28/37. The best line covers 35 cells, the first 28 of them still look solvable.
Generation 5: fitness 28/37. The best line covers 35 cells, the first 28 of them still look solvable.
Generation 7: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 7: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 72 futures: 96% survive going down-right (best covers 76%); up-left 33%; left 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 100% survive going up-left (best covers 73%); left 0%.
Tried 72 futures: 92% survive going right (best covers 76%); down-left 0%; down-right 0%.
Jackpot! A future covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 3,175 variables and 8,628 clauses in 0.07 s (867 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.01 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
